reply_text:
I found one statement from 2017 that fits: Zuckerberg said during his Facebook Live on 23 July 2017 that AI would improve lives "in the next five to 10 years." I only saw those words in a news report that quotes him and embeds the video, not in a Facebook transcript or the recording itself, so it is labelled coverage-only.

- **The Facebook Live statement.** He was answering a viewer's question about Elon Musk's AI warnings. RealClearPolitics quotes him: "I think that people who are naysayers and try to drum up these doomsday scenarios — I just, I don't understand it. I think it's really negative and in some ways I actually think it is pretty irresponsible. Because in the next five to 10 years, AI is going to deliver so many improvements in the quality of our lives." The 23 July date comes from search snippets, not a page I opened. A CNBC snippet said he broadcast on a Sunday afternoon, and the RealClearPolitics article is dated 25 July. That's why the JSON gives only "2017-07".
- **Lines I left out because they give no real date:**
  - His February 2017 essay "Building Global Community" says of Facebook's systems for flagging content, "It will take many years to fully develop these systems."
  - On the earnings call for the first quarter of 2017, he said better AI moderation "will take a period of years though to really reach the quality level that we want."
  - Both phrases are vague and neither is about AGI, so neither goes under candidates or undated.
- **Other occasions I checked:** The third-quarter earnings call's "over the next 10 years" describes Facebook's own work plan, not something AI will achieve. Nothing in Zuckerberg's own parts of the April F8 keynote transcript is a dated AI prediction. The second-quarter call transcript was behind a paywall, and I didn't open the Harvard commencement speech. I used 9 of 12 searches and all 6 page openings.
